{{Quote|Dual-phase blades seem to be something of a fad among Jedi at certain points.|Luke Skywalker|<ref name="IJ" />}}
A '''dual-phase lightsaber''' was a special variant of [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] that used one or a combination of [[Lightsaber crystal/Legends|focusing crystals]] to create a blade that could extend up to triple the original length with a simple activation. Unlike typical lightsabers, which often possessed a manual adjuster for reducing the blade emission, the dual-phased blade could be triggered in an instant, adding an element of surprise to catch an opponent off guard. Additionally, some dual-phase lightsabers also had a blade-width adjust. [[Gantoris]] wielded such a lightsaber,<ref name="DA" /> as did [[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]].<ref name="IJ" /> Dual phase lightsabers could also have the ability to carry different crystals, and alternate between them at the user's discretion.<ref name="DA" />

==History==
Records from circa [[400 BBY/Legends|400 BBY]] indicate that [[Keiran Halcyon]] constructed a special dual phase lightsaber that could go from the standard 1.3 meters to a length of three meters with flick of a switch. Most dual phase lightsabers date from the [[Jedi Civil War]], when lightsaber duels were common and the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] were at the height of their power. As more beings became aware of the Jedi fighting skills and the Jedi themselves strove to end disputes without drawing their weapons, duels grew less frequent and dual-phase lightsabers went out of style.<ref name="IJ" /> However, around the time of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], they began to see use again from both Jedi and Sith alike. [[Dooku/Legends|Count Dooku]] famously used one once he earned the title of Jedi Master, and presumably kept the functionality in his new lightsaber once he was named [[Sith Lord|Lord of the Sith]]. [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] also used a dual-phase [[Darth Vader's lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] after becoming Sith. However, unlike Count Dooku's curved hilt lightsaber, Vader used a more traditional straight hilt lightsaber. By the time of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] this style of lightsaber was so antiquated that they were considered a sign of old and outdated Jedi, which [[Ganner Rhysode]] frequently pointed out to [[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]] during their [[Mission to Bimmiel]]. In The Jedi Path, Grand Master [[Skarch Vaunk]] wrote that the weapon was only good for surprise attacks, and while that was not technically true the opinion pointed out that it was very rare for its time in the [[Rise of the Empire era]].<ref name="Jedi Path">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref>
